Alright, I've played this game since it was Operation Flashpoint. I've played about 1/2 the game modes, all the solo missions, hosted servers, and done a little bit of scripting. I've watched it change over the years, and not always for the better. I enjoy the game, but the changes over the last few years have been getting more and more questionable. And now what they've done is simply embarrassingly bad. Their last release "Contact" is essentially a $27 map, because it has almost no meaningful content whatsoever.

This is no longer a simulator. It has become a Bohemian Interactive fantasy. They've been so lazy that they have come to rely on former free material that was never right to begin with (Helicopters). Seriously, how can a company that got its start making simulations for military purposes completely fail with any measure of accuracy whatsoever? It isn't even about game balance, because its clear that was the least of their concerns. How? By so nerfing the game in general (missile ranges, lock-on capability, weapons damage), and the BLUEFOR side in particular (horrible tanks, weak 3rd party messed-up helicopters, completely nerfed CAS and fighter stats/capabilities), that it's clear where their interests lie. Still don't believe it? Play the Domination gamemode for BLUEFOR, and tell me you're not happy when you complete a side mission and get a decent vehicle FROM THE NEUTRAL FORCES instead of your own. How about those "mobile" AA launchers that aren't mobile at all? What's with this "turn off the engine, heat signature vanishes in minutes?" How about COMPLETE FAILURE TO COMPREHEND THAT THERMAL DOESN'T READ THROUGH GLASS? Seriously, anyone who actually believes that what they are seeing is an accurate simulation of capabilities would be dead long before they learned just how much fantasy is involved in the current abortive state.  

The game is enjoyable at times, and the maps are decent (but not $27 decent), but you really need to turn off all the BIS ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and play it modded. 

Just like with Ylands, Day Z, and everything else they've done in the last 5 years, this studio has worked very hard to become mediocre. And unlike with their releases, in that, they've succeeded amazingly well.
